Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer pricing follow-up

Thanks again for taking time on today's call, Erin — quick recap and next steps below.

Call recap:
- Use case: BrightCart search + summarization across product catalog and support docs (real-time API + some batch embedding jobs).
- Expected baseline: ~30M tokens/month with up to ~45M tokens/month peak during promotions.
- Desired commercial model: AWS/GCP/Azure marketplace private offer that maps to a per-unit token price ($/1M tokens) for ease of procurement.
- Important constraints: 12 month term preferred, ability to submit an AWS Private Offer, and predictable unit economics for cost allocation.

Open asks (can you confirm these so we align on pricing map):
1) Confirm typical monthly token baseline (you mentioned ~30M).
2) Confirm target budget range for LLM inference ($/month).
3) Is a single global unit price acceptable or do you need separate pricing by environment (prod/staging) or region?

What I'm sending next: an initial unit-price mapping (attached XLSX) that translates Redwood list/unit economics to marketplace private-offer list prices on AWS/GCP/Azure and shows the approximate $/1M-tokens you'd see on vendor invoices after marketplace fees. Highlights in the sheet:
- Suggested unit price targets across marketplaces (net to Redwood) and gross list price to set in the private offer (to account for marketplace take).
- Minimum commit / monthly spend scenarios (helps meet your budget guardrails).

Next steps:
- Erin: confirm the three items above and share the internal budget band you'd be comfortable with.
- Sarah: help us confirm typical AWS marketplace fee structure for private offers (we'll use 12% as a starting assumption unless you advise otherwise).
- We'll iterate the attached price map and follow with a proposed private offer and a PO template.

Attachments: BrightCart_PrivOffer_PriceMap.xlsx (spreadsheet, pricing scenarios)

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 15m follow-up if it helps.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0132

Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer pricing follow-up

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers inline below.

1) Baseline: we're comfortable with ~30M tokens/month for Q4 and expect an average of ~30M over the year with promotional peaks up to ~45M for 4-6 weeks.
2) Budget: currently we have a discretionary budget band for model inference of $18k–$30k/month. We could stretch for strategic features but want predictable unit economics.
3) Prefer a single unit price for prod across regions (we manage regional costs centrally). Staging/dev can be at a different (higher) unit price or discounted QA seat — not necessary in the private offer.

Target unit price: given internal benchmarks, we're targeting something around $600 per 1M tokens (net). If you can get us to ~500–600/1M with the private offer that would be ideal.

We can share an internal PO template if that helps; I see you attached one already.

--

Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer pricing follow-up

Thanks Erin — that's helpful. I pulled together an initial mapping and a few pricing options (see attached XLSX). Summary of the options (all prices shown as net to BrightCart in $ per 1M tokens, and gross list price you'd set in the private offer):

Option A — Conservative (recommended for predictable costs)
- Net unit price (what you effectively pay, after marketplace fees): $600 / 1M tokens
- Gross list price to set in AWS private offer (assuming 12% marketplace fee): $681 / 1M tokens
- Minimum commit: 12 months, 24M tokens/month commit (discount tiers above 40M)

Option B — Aggressive (higher commit, lower unit price)
- Net unit price: $520 / 1M tokens
- Gross list price: $590 / 1M tokens (assumes fee negotiation or marketplace promo credits)
- Minimum commit: 12 months, 40M tokens/month commit

Marketplace mapping notes:
- AWS: private offers require a list price on marketplace; AWS takes ~12% fee on the marketplace invoice (we used this for gross-to-net math).
- GCP: typically similar take rates but billing flows differ — we mapped an equivalent gross price in the sheet.
- Azure: marketplace pricing can be similar but there's occasionally an integration surcharge; see tab 3 in the sheet.

Unit economics and run-rate example (Option A):
- If you use 30M tokens/mo @ $600/1M = $18,000/mo (~$216k/year).
- Peak months (45M) = $27,000/mo.

Next steps I'm proposing:
1) Review the attached price map and tell us which option aligns with your procurement risk tolerance.
2) If Option A or B look good, we'll prepare an AWS Private Offer draft (we'll propose the gross list price) and a PO template for you to route internally.
3) Legal: attach our T&Cs (see redwood_tnc.docx). We can accept PO with signature + private offer confirmation.

Attachments: BrightCart_PrivOffer_PriceMap.xlsx, redwood_tnc.docx, PO_template.pdf

Happy to adjust assumptions if Sarah has a different fee figure.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0132

Subject: Fwd: Marketplace private offer pricing follow-up — internal note

Quick internal note — copying key context from the thread. Thoughts:

- Erin's target net $600/1M with 30M baseline gives us revenue of ~$18k/mo. With current cost profiles (model + infra + SRE ops) and estimated cost savings from batching/KV-cache we estimate gross margin around 55–60% at that price point for hosted inference. After marketplace fee (12%) the gross to us is slightly lower — our modeling in the XLSX assumes ~20% total pass-through/fee + infra cost.

- If we want to protect margin and still be competitive in marketplace private offers, I recommend we:
  * Push for Option A as default (net $600) with a 12-month term and minimum 24M tokens/mo.
  * Offer Option B (net $520) only with 40M+ commit and a 12-month term — include an annual true-up clause.

Next steps for us: finance POV (Nikhil) to confirm acceptable minimum unit, prepare pricing worksheet for deal desk, and legal to review the T&Cs before we send the private-offer draft.

-Aditya
